newsitem.title: USA: Clinton, Dole teams bicker over debates.
newsitem.headline: Clinton, Dole teams bicker over debates.

text.p: Aides to President Clinton and Bob Dole bickered on Wednesday over when to resume talks on the format of presidential debates, as each side charged the other was creating scheduling problems.

Clinton's chief negotiator, Mickey Kantor, declared on Cable News Network that he wanted to get together again "as soon as possible" with the Dole negotiators headed by former South Carolina Gov. Carroll Campbell to set up the debates.
But Dole aides countered that Kantor, who is commerce secretary, had caused scheduling difficulties.
"I'm suggesting getting together as soon as possible ... it could be this afternoon," Kantor said on CNN.

Kantor said he spoke with Campbell by telephone on Wednesday and asked for a meeting, but Campbell had said he would call Kantor back in 36 hours. "So I'm waiting by the phone, holding my breath," Kantor said.
Donald Rumsfeld, Dole's national campaign chairman who appeared with Kantor, countered that Kantor said previously he could not schedule any debate talks for Thursday or Friday.
"And now, he for the first time has announced that he has cancelled his plans," Rumsfeld said. "This is brand new information and it's just plain politics."

Campbell had a scheduling conflict that prevented him from meeting Kantor on Wednesday, said Campbell's spokeswoman Ginny Bueno. She said he was in a board meeting of the American Council of Life Insurance, of which he is president.
Officials in the Dole campaign said it might be Saturday before their negotiators finally meet again, although Kantor said "its got to be earlier than that."

Kantor, Campbell and other members of their negotiating teams met on Tuesday for more than two hours but the session ended with no resolution of outstanding issues such as how many debates and how long they should be.
The first debate had been tentatively scheduled by the Commission on Presidential Debates for Sept. 25 -- a week away -- in St. Louis. But the odds of that happening appeared slimmer than ever.

A major point of contention was whether third party candidate Ross Perot should be excluded as the Commission on Presidential Debates recommended on Tuesday. The Clinton forces have proposed that Perot be included in one debate; the Dole forces were resisting this.

"It's certainly clear that we want to reach out to the supporters of Ross Perot even if that candidate isn't in the debate," Dole spokesman Nelson Warfield, travelling with the candidate in California, said on Wednesday.
"Our position remains the same. We're anxious to debate. We're anxious and ready to go, starting in St. Louis on the 25th or 26th (of September)," said Warfield.
Clinton's aides have said he cannot participate on Sept. 25, because of a speech he was scheduled to give at the United Nations the day before.

Kantor says his side wants two presidential and one vice presidential debate, all between Oct. 6-13. In addition to including Perot in the first presidential debate, he was pressing for Perot's running mate Pat Choate to be included in the vice presidential debate.
The Dole campaign wants three presidential and one vice presidential debate, each 75 minutes long and with a single moderator, and all excluding Perot and Choate.
